body: Batticaloa Fort is a historic fort in the town of Batticaloa in Sri Lanka. It was built by the Portuguese in 1628 and was captured by the Dutch in 1638. The fort is protected by the Batticaloa Lagoon on two sides and a canal on the other two sides. It has a structure of four bastions and is surrounded by a moat.The fort is now used by the Sri Lankan government as a district secretariat. However, it is still open to visitors and is a popular tourist destination. The fort offers stunning views of the lagoon and the surrounding town. There are also a number of cannons on display within the fort, which provide a glimpse into its rich history.Pros:* The fort is well-maintained and clean.* The views from the ramparts are stunning.* There are a number of cannons on display within the fort.* The fort is a popular tourist destination, so there are plenty of opportunities to interact with locals.Cons:* The fort is not very large, so it can be explored in a short amount of time.* The fort is currently used by the Sri Lankan government, so some areas may be off-limits to visitors.* There is no admission fee, so the fort can get crowded, especially on weekends.Overall, Batticaloa Fort is a worthwhile visit for anyone interested in history or architecture. It is a beautiful and well-maintained fort that offers stunning views of the surrounding area. However, it is not very large, so it may not be a good choice for those looking for a long and detailed exploration.**Recommendation:I would recommend visiting Batticaloa Fort in the morning or late afternoon, when the crowds are smaller. You can also take a boat ride around the lagoon to get a different perspective of the fort. If you are interested in learning more about the history of the fort, there are a number of guides available who can provide more information.
title: A fort in Batticaloa...

body: It is one of the medium size Dutch Forts in Sri Lanka having immense architectural value. The old buildings within, even though needing further restoration or conservation are still in active use. Dating back to 1682 the fort structure has shielded itself well against natural elements from damaging it. Forts are the key landmarks that are remaining of the Portuguese and Dutch occupation of Sri Lanka along the coastal regions. These sturdy built Forts, each one has its own character and a construction history depending on the location where they have been built. Similarly Batticoloa fort has been built with loads of Granite stone and brick.After entering the premises through the the main gate, there is a wooden staircase to walk up to the rampart. Rampart is colonised by naturally growing grasses but a clear walk way was kept well trimmed so that a visitor could walk the entire circuit without any difficulty. Views from the rampart was vivid. From One direction it was the Kallady bridge, from another the lagoon spanning several kilometres, from another the moat surrounding the rampart was visible. The guard houses at the corners and a structure which could be a bell tower remains on the rampart. A British era cannon moulded with ER insignia gives an idea to how it would have been during the days of its glory. Those who appreciate sites with historic heritage will enjoy taking a tour, walking on the rampart around the fort. If authorities give real value to this site it will be an excellent attraction! Proper signage to guide the visitor's is of prime importance.
title: A fort with lot of charm and character

body: People call The Dutch Fort but originally it was build by the Portuguese in early 16th centuries and captured by the Dutch. I was born in Batticaloa somewhere a couple of KM from the fort so I know quite a lot of story about this fort. This fort is not as wonderful as red fort in Delhi or many others around the world. But it has a lot of stories not only about the western colony but also the story of civil war in Sri Lanka.People who wants to visit the fort first must understand the whole story of Sri Lanka. East and North part of Sri Lanka was not a touristic place just a few years ago but a war zone. Batticaloa was one of the city which suffered the most by the civil war and the Tsunami. The most important issue was for the people here in their day to day life is to survive. They had no clue when it would be their chance. While some other city like Galle in the south was already receiving a large amount of foreigners and well prepared nicely organized.Batticaloa fort is protected by the Batticaloa Lagoon on two sides and a canal on the other two sides. This was one of the main reason the local administration moved in to the fort for safety reason during the civil war. The fort and the surroundings were in the high security zone during the civil war. Part of the fort was also occupied by the Sri Lankan Army 232 Brigade. During this period the fort was not accessible for public. Everywhere barbed wire and even land mines were planted by the SL army in order to protect the 232 brigade and the high court. This is one of the reason people are still afraid to even go and clean the areas. In my point of view this fort is not about to compare with others sites. Every historical sites has its own story and identity. You should understand first what are the story behind this little fort and then who are the people lives around and what they have been gone through for quite 3 decades. And now you all have the opportunity to enter in to the fort and imagine what it could have been if the civil war in Sri Lanka wasn't over; maybe it could have been completely destroyed and no longer existing. Apart from the story you can have a nice walk along the lagoon or even have a boat ride to the light house. Really worth a visit if you have a couple of hours.
title: A historical place go only if you know the history

body: The fort is the oldest extant structure in Batticaloa, and it does have a picturesque charm about it. On can easily imagine Dutch man-of-wars sailing into the lagoon and heading for the fort, cannons at the ready. So although the fort is small, it is charming.The keep is built up with modern buildings that are used as offices for local government; the inside is nicely maintained and worth taking a quick look. It would make a lovely high-end hotel space. There are two staircases; find one and carefully climb them to walk the walls; great views of the area surrounding Batti. And while on the walls, don't forget to glimpse through the doors into the offices there; you're sure to see several government workers, or idling on their smartphones; it's the closest thing Batti has to a zoo.
title: Come, walk the walls and see government workers sleeping at their desks.

body: The Batticaloa fort is a small fort. It was (like most forts on the island) build by the Portuguese (1628) and captured by the Dutch in 1638. It became English in 1745, but the Dutch VOC sign is still at the entrance gate. There is a nice statue of two fishes holding a book. This book gives a description of the history from the fort. Inside there are new buildings from the local government. The walls are still in a quite good condition and there is an old English cannon on the walls facing the lagoon. It would be a good idea for the local people to clean the place up, because it does have some touristic potential. At the moment it’s interesting for Dutch people and people who are interested in history. But it’s not a highlight.

title: Intact wall
body: This Fort was built by the Portugese in 1628 and helps to explain why the are so many Catholics in the area.While the colonial era buildings inside are now used by government authorities as diverse as the Census entity and the Army, there are apparently to convert it to tourism given that Sri Lanka has enjoyed peace since 2009.The outer wall has a lovely section fronting the lagoon that would look great if incorporated into an exclusive hotel.The soldiers gave our Australian group permission to enter. There is a post iffice near the gate that sells R25 international postcard stamps.
